newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to cut 97 welfare gap to 29.7 bln - Barrot.
newsitem.headline: France to cut 97 welfare gap to 29.7 bln - Barrot.

text.p: The French government expects to reduce the welfare deficit next year to 29.7 billion francs through control of spending and increases in taxes and excise duties, Labour and Social Affairs minister Jacques Barrot said on Monday.
He was speaking at a news conference after the social security accounts commission forecast a deficit of 47 billion next year without new measures, after a deficit of 51.6 billion this year.
The government is to present a bill to parliament shortly on reforming finance for the social security system, which uses mostly payroll charges to fund health care, pensions and family benefits.
"There is between the forecast and the 29.7 billion franc target a margin in which political will must intervene," Barrot told a news conference.
